evals.prompt: Run a full telx-review of this repo. We're about to open it up to outside contributors and I want to know what is actually wrong before they see it: anything that could cost an LP money, anything that could leak our API keys, and the UX, UI, and performance problems worth fixing first.
evals.expected_output: A verified review report (report-<branch>.md) covering all seven angles with a toolchain section, a findings table with verification status, file:line locations, proposed fixes for confirmed findings, a coverage section, and a short conversation summary with verification statistics and grouped action items.
expectations: A markdown review report exists in outputs/ with Toolchain, Summary, Findings, and Coverage sections
Every finding has a Location of the form file_path:line_number where the file exists in the repo and the line is within the file
Every non-Informational finding carries a verification status (Confirmed, False positive, Design decision, Partially valid, or Not verified), not just an initial severity
Findings or coverage notes span at least five of the seven angles: web3 safety, app security, data correctness, UX, UI, performance, best practices
Every confirmed Critical or High finding includes a proposed fix that contains code
The report states the result of the type check, lint, tests, and build, and those results match an independent run of the same commands
No standalone finding restates a CONTRIBUTING.md known gap (Prettier not installed, permissive lint rules, deprecated next lint, missing tests) without adding a concrete new defect
Severity labels use the dapp scale (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational) and no finding is justified with blockchain-node concepts such as consensus or validators
The final conversation summary reports verification statistics (findings submitted versus confirmed) and action items grouped by severity
At least one verified finding concerns the money path (transaction construction, approvals, decimals, or reward amounts) with a location in src/web3, src/merkl, src/lib/tokens.ts, or src/helpers

The report contains at least 6 of these 8 issues, each verified true against the code on 2026-09-25: legacy staking transactions sent without a chain check; the dfx route interpolating poolAddress into a URL that carries the backend bearer secret; the faulty-contract Withdraw throwing on ethers v5 .gt() over a v6 bigint; Merkl and legacy Uniswap claims reporting success without reading receipt.status; Uniswap v4 subscribe sent without a chainId; the Alchemy key shipped in the client bundle; next 15.5.9 carrying open advisories; /portfolio crashing on an empty rewards array
The report itself (not only the chat summary) carries a prioritised action list grouped by severity

evals.prompt: review the changes on this branch against main before I open the PR
evals.expected_output: A diff-scoped review: scope.md listing changed files and their importers, only the relevant angles spawned, a verified report on the branch's changes with file:line locations and fixes, and a toolchain section.
expectations: A scope file lists the files changed against main and the files that import them
Only angles whose file map intersects the changed files are spawned, and the report says which ran
Every finding cites a file:line inside the changed files or their importers
The report carries verification status per finding and a toolchain section

evals.prompt: look at the merkl claim flow (src/merkl plus the merkl-user-rewards api route). is there anything that could send a claim to the wrong place, show the wrong reward amount, or leave a user stuck after clicking claim?
evals.expected_output: An area-scoped review that runs at least web3-safety, data-correctness, app-security, and ux, with verified findings on the Merkl distributor address per chain, token and decimals handling, proof and input validation in the route handler, and pending/error feedback in the claim UI.
expectations: The review runs at least the web3-safety, data-correctness, app-security, and ux angles
The Merkl Distributor address and per-chain handling are examined, with a file:line in src/merkl
Token and decimals handling in the reward filter is examined (symbol versus address match, 18 decimals)
Input validation in src/app/api/merkl-user-rewards/route.ts is examined
Pending, error, and rejection feedback in the claim UI is examined
Every finding presented as confirmed went through verification
